qAndA.answer: The adjustment layer acts as a container for the effects used to create the transition, allowing them to be applied to a specific portion of the video without affecting the original clips.
qAndA.question: What is the purpose of the adjustment layer in this transition effect?

qAndA.answer: Setting the Shutter Angle to 360 degrees maximizes the motion blur applied by the Transform effect, creating a smoother and more visually appealing zoom blur.
qAndA.question: Why does the narrator set the 'Shutter Angle' to 360 degrees?

qAndA.answer: The narrator adjusts the keyframes for Scale in the Graph Editor to give the animation a smooth curve, avoiding abrupt changes in speed and creating a more natural zooming effect.
qAndA.question: What keyframe changes are made in the Graph Editor, and why?

qAndA.answer: Setting the direction to 90 degrees ensures that the motion blur follows the horizontal zoom movement, enhancing the feeling of rapid movement and contributing to a more seamless transition.
qAndA.question: What is the effect of setting the 'Direction' of the blur to 90 degrees?

qAndA.answer: The narrator applies the 'Easy Ease' function to the keyframes of the Blur Length, further refining the animation curve and achieving a smoother and more gradual change in the amount of motion blur.
qAndA.question: How does the narrator recommend smoothing out the motion blur animation?

timecoded_text_to_speech.text: As you can see I've already got my clips on the timeline, but we don't have a transition yet,
we're going to make one. Right click here, new adjustment layer. Let's cut the adjustment layer
5 frames to the left and do the same for the right side to 5 frames to the right, total of 10 frames
for adjustment layer. Delete the excess parts and bring the playhead in between the clips.
Go to effects and presets, search for Transform and add it to the adjustment layer.
Here make sure to uncheck use composition's shadow angle and set the shadow angle to 360
to get the maximum amount of motion blur. Then create a keyframe for scale, press U to reveal
the keyframes and move that keyframe to the beginning of the adjustment layer. Create another one,
and drag that keyframe to the end of the adjustment layer and set the scale to 300 for the middle point.
Then select all the keyframes, press F9 and go to the graph editor. Here we need to adjust the graph
editor accordingly to get the smoothest and the snappiest animation. Just repeat my steps and give
this graph a curve like this. Once you do it, exit the graph editor and you're ready to preview
our transition. Most people will be satisfied with how this transition looks already,
but we're going to give it my motion blur. Search for the effect direction blur, add it to the
adjustment layer. The move the playhead in between the clips. The go to effect control, set direction
to 90 degrees, create a keyframe for blur length, press U a couple times to see the keyframes
for the direction of blur, move that keyframe to the start, create another one and move it to the
end. Then for the middle point here, increase blur length to however you like it, I'll set it to 100
and select all the keyframes, press F9 to ease those keyframes and let's preview it. So as you can
see now our animation has a lot more motion blur to it, it looks more seamless. That was pretty much
our tutorial, if you enjoyed, give this video a like and also subscribe to my channel because I
post a lot of videos like this. Thank you so much for watching, I'll see you in the next video.
